place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 228-236 George Avenue

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; the first standardised housing on the base: a side-gabled block with a full two-storey columned front porch and balcony, a tall chimney, 6/6 windows, on a long straight street of identical houses with a water tower at the end.

facade.notes: a streetscape on the base: two-storey brick duplexes with full front porches on columns, set evenly along a street with a sidewalk, a terrace of grown street trees, utility poles and a cobra-head street light; the water tower over the roofs

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
1920s-30s military housing used Colonial Revival brick for dignity and economy (Quartermaster standard plans)
a planned base street: uniform setbacks and a regular row of street trees
